page.h1: Best iPhone case for protection: OtterBox Defender Series Pro, and how to read drop ratings
page.desc: Our pick for iPhone drop protection is the OtterBox Defender Series Pro. Here is what 7X, 6X, 24 ft and 25 ft drop ratings count, with maker prices checked on 2026-11-10.
page.answer: Short answer. The best protective iPhone case is the OtterBox Defender Series Pro: its 7X military drop protection rating means 182 drops from 4 ft, not a height. UAG Monarch Pro's 25 ft and SUPCASE UB Pro's 20 ft are drop heights, so the two kinds of rating can't be ranked against each other.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • OtterBox Defender Series Pro: 7 × 26 drops = 182 drops, each from the test's 4 ft (48 in). OtterBox publishes no drop height above 4 ft.
  • Pelican Shield MagSafe: 6 × 4 ft = 24 ft. Pelican's "6X" multiplies the height, while OtterBox's 7X multiplies the number of drops.
  • UAG Monarch Pro: 25 ft ÷ 4 ft = 6.25. That isn't 5, so UAG's "5X MIL-SPEC" can't be a height multiple, and UAG doesn't say what it counts.
  • Smartish Gripmunk: 50 drops from 6 ft onto concrete. It is the only rating here that gives the number of drops, the height and the surface.
  • Cost per rated foot of drop height: UAG $42.95 ÷ 25 ft = $1.72; SUPCASE UB Pro $39.99 ÷ 20 ft = $2.00; UB Grip Pro $43.99 ÷ 20 ft = $2.20; Pelican $69.99 ÷ 24 ft = $2.92. The Defender has no height rating, so it has no per-foot figure.
  • Weight: SUPCASE lists the UB Pro for the iPhone 17 Pro at 147.8 g. iDrop News gives the Spigen Tough Armor T as 1.8 oz (≈51 g). 147.8 ÷ 51 ≈ 2.9, so the UB Pro weighs about three times as much.

What '7X' and '25 ft' actually measure

The military standard these cases cite, MIL-STD-810 Method 516, is a transit-drop test. The item is dropped 26 times from 48 in (122 cm), once on each face, edge and corner, onto 2 in of plywood over concrete. The 26 drops may be spread across as many as five test units, so a single case doesn't have to survive all of them.

OtterBox's DROP+ scale treats that test as 1X (26 drops from 4 ft) and counts up from there: 2X = 52, 5X = 130, 7X = 182. OtterBox's VP of Engineering, Doug Kempel, says the 7X Defender Series Pro survived "over 180 drops". In other words, OtterBox tests many drops from about the height a phone falls from a hand or pocket. UAG states a single figure instead: "independently tested to withstand drops up to 25 feet". It names no lab, surface or number of drops. Pelican's "24ft [6X]" is also a height. Neither kind of number can be converted into the other, so the box ratings alone can't rank these cases.

One independent result exists for the pick. In the Good Housekeeping Institute's lab drop tester, the Defender Series Pro left the test phone unscathed.

The front glass is what breaks. In Allstate Protection Plans' drop test, reported by Notebookcheck, an iPhone 17 Pro's front glass shattered on a 6 ft face-down drop, while a back-down drop left only cosmetic damage. If your case's listing doesn't put a screen protector in the box (both SUPCASE models here include one), add a glass screen protector.

Not recommended

SUPCASE Unicorn Beetle Pro if you use MagSafe. SUPCASE's own listing says the UB Pro "does NOT support MagSafe", so magnetic chargers, wallets and car mounts won't hold. It also fits only the size printed on the box (18 Pro / 17 Pro, or 18 Pro Max / 17 Pro Max), not the base iPhone 17. If you need MagSafe, SUPCASE's UB Grip Pro MagSafe costs $4 more ($43.99 vs $39.99) and carries the same 20 ft claim.
